issues.issue: Whether the illegality of the Iraq war is relevant under paragraph 171 of the UN Handbook (certified question)
issues.applicant_position: Appellants: illegality of the Iraq war is relevant to paragraph 171, so evidence on it should have been admitted.
issues.result_quote: I would therefore decline to answer the certified question

issues.issue: Whether the appellants rebutted the presumption of state protection where the state is alleged to be the persecutor
issues.applicant_position: Appellants: state protection is absent where the state itself is the persecutor, so no need to show it was sought.
issues.respondent_position: Not stated as argument; Board and Federal Court held the presumption of state protection not rebutted.
issues.result_quote: applies equally to cases where an individual claims to fear persecution by non-state entities and to cases where the state is alleged to be a persecutor

issues.issue: Whether the appellants made objectively reasonable efforts to seek US protection (Ward and Kadenko) before claiming refugee status
issues.applicant_position: Appellants: US protection was not reasonably forthcoming; conscientious objection covers only specific wars; Executive appeal illusory.
issues.respondent_position: Not stated as argument; Board and Federal Court held the appellants did not exhaust US protections.
issues.result_quote: I find that it was objectively unreasonable for the appellants to have failed to take significant steps

issues.issue: Whether the Board's finding that the appellants would face imprisonment for desertion ignored the evidence that most deserters are not prosecuted
issues.applicant_position: Appellants say one to five years imprisonment for desertion would amount to persecution.
issues.respondent_position: Not stated as argument; Board relied on likely imprisonment, which the Court finds was made without regard to key statistics.
issues.result_quote: its opinion regarding the punishment the appellants will potentially face upon return to the United States was made without regard to the material before it

issues.issue: Whether the wife's and son's refugee claims succeed as members of Mr. Hinzman's immediate family
issues.applicant_position: Wife and son claimed as immediate family (particular social group); no separate arguments were advanced.
issues.result_quote: Since Mr. Hinzman has failed to establish his claim, their claims must also fail.
